# Finly

Finly is Bruce Wen's solo submission to the Alpaca AI Trading Agents Hackathon. It is an educational paper-trading research prototype, not investment advice.

## Judge-facing proposition

Finly separates the right to interpret market evidence from the right to expose capital. An AI component may produce a bounded assessment and rationale. Deterministic code owns direction, horizon, sizing, defined-risk option construction, challenge tests, and the final PERMIT or NO_TRADE decision. Broker authority is disabled by default.

## Strongest quantitative evidence

- A nonproduction research shadow called G4 was tested in a consumed adjusted-close ETF replay from 2013-01-02 through 2026-08-27.
- A modeled $100,000 ended at $1,067,106 for G4 versus $680,817 for SPY: a $386,289 historical difference.
- G4 returned 18.97% annualized versus 15.11% for SPY.
- G4 maximum drawdown was -28.99% versus -33.72% for SPY.
- The replay applies a modeled 5-basis-point one-way turnover cost.
- The website contains an interactive range explorer that recomputes standalone entry and exit costs for a selected period.
- Across the full consumed record, G4 beat SPY in all 2,175 overlapping five-year trading-session windows. These windows overlap heavily and are descriptive, not independent trials.

## Evidence boundary

G4 was selected after historical results were viewed. It is not the production Finly policy, a forward forecast, an options-profit record, or proof of future profitability. It remains a nonproduction shadow because statistical and source-overlap promotion gates failed. Production Finly has zero forward performance observations. The repository does not claim guaranteed profit or likely next-month SPY outperformance.

## Verification

From a clean clone with Node.js 22.13 or newer: `npm install && npm run verify`.

The public evidence is designed to be evaluated against the cited project artifacts and explicit claim boundaries.
